name: Saints Cosmas and Damian
bio: Tradition presents Cosmas and Damian as brothers born in Arabia who studied medicine in Syria and cared for the sick without charging anything. The Eastern Church therefore calls them the anargyroi, "those who take no money".

They were put to death as Christians in the persecution of Diocletian, early in the fourth century. Their cult spread early through the East and to Rome, and their names entered the Roman Canon of the Mass. They are patrons of physicians, surgeons and pharmacists.
why: Cosmas and Damian are a reminder that caring for those who suffer, competently and without turning another's pain into a business, is already a way of proclaiming the Gospel.
prayer: Saints Cosmas and Damian, pray for us.

name: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, Archangels
bio: Scripture names three archangels. Michael, "who is like God?", appears in the Book of Daniel and in Revelation as the one who fights evil; the Church invokes him as a defender. Gabriel, "strength of God", is the messenger who announces to Zechariah the birth of John and to Mary the incarnation of the Son.

Raphael, "God heals", accompanies young Tobias in the Book of Tobit, heals his father and presents himself as one of the seven who stand before the Lord. Since the 1969 reform of the calendar the three are celebrated together on 29 September. Pius XII proclaimed Gabriel patron of telecommunications in 1951.
why: The archangels say that God does not govern from afar: he protects in the struggle, speaks at the decisive moment and walks alongside, even to healing.
prayer: Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, pray for us.
fonte: Vatican News, Santo do dia: https://www.vaticannews.va/pt/santo-do-dia/09/29.html; Tb 12,15; Lc 1,19.26; Ap 12,7

name: Saint Jerome
role: Priest and Doctor of the Church
bio: Jerome was born in Stridon, in Dalmatia, to a Christian family, and studied in Rome. He lived as a hermit in the desert of Chalcis, near Aleppo, where he deepened his Greek and learned Hebrew. In 382 he became secretary to Pope Damasus, who asked him for a new Latin translation of the biblical texts.

In 386 he settled in Bethlehem, where, with the support of the Roman noblewoman Paula, he founded a monastery for men, one for women and a hostel for pilgrims. There he revised the Gospels and the Psalter and translated most of the Old Testament from Hebrew: the Vulgate, which became the Church's official Latin text. He died in Bethlehem on 30 September 419 or 420.
why: Jerome is the source of the line "ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ". He is a reminder that reading the Bible with attention and study, not only out of habit, is a way to know Jesus.
fonte: Benedict XVI, General Audience of 7 November 2007: https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/audiences/2007/documents/hf_ben-xvi_aud_20071107.html

name: Saint Faustina Kowalska
role: Religious sister, apostle of Divine Mercy
bio: Helena Kowalska was born in Głogowiec, Poland, on 25 August 1905, the third of ten children in a poor and devout family. In 1925 she entered the Congregation of the Sisters of Our Lady of Mercy in Warsaw and received the name Sister Maria Faustina. She worked as a cook, gardener and porter in several of the congregation's houses.

In her Diary she recorded the words she attributed to Jesus and the request to spread trust in God's mercy, with the image of the Merciful Jesus. She died of tuberculosis in Kraków on 5 October 1938, aged 33. John Paul II beatified her in 1993 and canonized her on 30 April 2000, when he instituted Divine Mercy Sunday.
why: Faustina shows that a hidden life, in simple tasks and with frail health, can carry a message for the whole Church: no one is too far from God's mercy.
fonte: Vatican News, St. Faustina Kowalska: https://www.vaticannews.va/en/saints/10/05/st--faustina-kowalska.html; João Paulo II, Homilia da canonização, 30 de abril de 2000: https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/homilies/2000/documents/hf_jp-ii_hom_20000430_faustina.html

name: Saint Bruno
bio: Bruno was born in Cologne around 1030 and was a teacher and head of the cathedral school in Reims. In mid-life he left his career and, in 1084, withdrew with six companions to the Chartreuse massif in the Alps, where he began the life of silence and solitude that gave the Carthusian Order its name.

Six years later Pope Urban II, his former student, called him to Rome as an adviser. Bruno declined the archbishopric of Reggio and asked to return to solitude; he founded a new hermitage in Calabria, where he died on 6 October 1101.
why: Bruno is a reminder that silence is not a flight from the world: it is a place where one learns to listen to God. A little of that silence fits into any routine.

name: Saint John XXIII
bio: Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli was born in Sotto il Monte, near Bergamo, on 25 November 1881, into a farming family. Ordained in 1904, he was secretary to the Bishop of Bergamo, a chaplain in the First World War and later the Holy See's representative in Bulgaria, Turkey and Greece, and nuncio in France. In 1953 he became Patriarch of Venice.

Elected pope on 28 October 1958, he convoked the Second Vatican Council, opened on 11 October 1962, the date chosen for his memorial. Among other encyclicals he wrote Pacem in terris. He died on 3 June 1963, was beatified by John Paul II in 2000 and canonized by Pope Francis on 27 April 2014.
why: John XXIII became known as "the good pope": firm in faith and open to dialogue. He shows that goodness and the courage to renew can go together.
prayer: Saint John XXIII, pray for us.
fonte: Santa Sé, Biographical Profile of Pope John XXIII: https://www.vatican.va/content/john-xxiii/en/biography/documents/hf_j-xxiii_bio_20190722_biografia.html

name: Saint Ignatius of Antioch
bio: Ignatius was the third bishop of Antioch, in Syria. Under the emperor Trajan he was arrested and taken under guard to Rome, to be thrown to the beasts. On the journey he wrote seven letters: to the Churches of Ephesus, Magnesia, Tralles, Rome, Philadelphia and Smyrna, and to Bishop Polycarp.

In them he insists on the unity of Christians around the bishop and the Eucharist, and he is the first Christian writer to use the expression "Catholic Church". He died a martyr in Rome around the year 107.
why: Ignatius wrote about unity when everything pushed him toward fear. He teaches that communion in the Church is defended with one's life, not only with ideas.
prayer: Saint Ignatius of Antioch, pray for us.
fonte: Benedict XVI, General Audience of 14 March 2007: https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/audiences/2007/documents/hf_ben-xvi_aud_20070314.html

name: Saint Luke
bio: Luke is the author of the third Gospel and of the Acts of the Apostles. Paul calls him "the beloved physician" in the Letter to the Colossians, and he was Paul's travelling companion. At the start of his Gospel he says he investigated everything carefully from the beginning in order to write an orderly account.

His Gospel keeps the parables of mercy, such as the prodigal son and the good Samaritan, and the accounts of Jesus' infancy. Tradition made him patron of artists and calls him the "painter" of Our Lady, perhaps for the care with which he portrays people.
why: Luke writes like someone who cares: attentive to the poor, to women and to sinners. Reading his Gospel is learning Jesus' merciful way of looking at people.
fonte: Vatican News, Santo do dia: https://www.vaticannews.va/pt/santo-do-dia/10/18.html; Cl 4,14; Lc 1,1-4; At 1,1
